hypotheses.claim: A dual curriculum of census-derived cognitive-process trajectories plus an isolated dynamic-binding micro-skill lane, composed only where routing is semantically natural, should generalize better than either binder-only or trajectory-only training.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: apparent gain could come from shared schemas, lexical cues or Claude/DB vocabulary rather than reusable cognitive process semantics.
hypotheses.discriminator: freeze family/provenance splits first; compare binder-only, trajectory-only and selective-composition checkpoints on unseen process families, unseen codebook permutations, variable-N invariance, DB-vs-simulation lesions, Claude handoff/re-entry and retention floors. Aggregate gain cannot hide a failed channel.

hypotheses.claim: cognitive process identity should remain stable across N and executor replacement while scheduling/resource outputs may change equivariantly with N and capacity.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: forcing full output invariance across N would erase legitimate load/capacity-sensitive coordination behavior.
hypotheses.discriminator: score semantic process/state identity separately from N-sensitive scheduling decisions using matched N=1/10/20 and resize-during-task families.

hypotheses.claim: split-clean Hyperposition decodability is necessary but insufficient; useful carrier acceptance requires matched behavioral/OOD use plus selective causal intervention or the strongest exposed equivalent.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: a decodable subspace may be epiphenomenal or intervention-sensitive only through an off-path/dormant mechanism.
hypotheses.discriminator: representation -> behavior -> lesion/shuffle/rescue or matched intervention -> scope-bounded re-entry evidence, with fresh preregistered holdout and off-target controls.
